item.title: C++ Crash Reporting & Stack Trace Libraries: backward-cpp vs Breakpad vs Crashpad
item.description: When your C++ application crashes in production, the default experience is a cryptic SIGSEGV with no context. Was it a null pointer? Buffer overflow? Use-after-free? Without a stack trace, you’re debugging blind. Crash reporting and backtrace libraries capture the call stack at the moment of failure — turning “it crashed” into “it crashed at ConnectionPool::reconnect(), called from HealthChecker::run(), with this=0x0.”
